children: The annual growth rate of lending to Swedish households held at 3.3% in August 2026, unchanged from July and remaining at its highest level since December 2022.
Housing loans, which accounted for 83% of total household credit, grew 3.5%, while consumer loans, representing 6%, increased 1.4%.
Meanwhile, lending to non-financial corporations expanded 3.9%.
Borrowing costs remained broadly lower, with the average interest rate on new housing loan agreements steady at 2.78%, while the average floating mortgage rate edged down to 2.73% from 2.74%.
The average fixed rate for new housing loans with maturities of one to five years rose to 3.18% from 3.15%, while rates for maturities above five years increased to 3.34% from 3.21%.
Total household deposits edged up to SEK 2,970 billion from SEK 2,967 billion, with demand deposits accounting for 74% of savings at SEK 2,202 billion.

title: Swedish Household Lending Growth Holds at Highest Since 2022
